scope: Public content inspection and independently written rule mapping. No external code executed, no paid full text, no configuration changes.

literature.title: NASA-STD-7009B: Standard for Models and Simulations
literature.reading_scope: 88-page public PDF: definitions and sections 4.1-4.3, especially printed/PDF pp25,28-30,32-33; p28 visually verified.
verified_content: Records units and vector frames (M&S46); assumptions, abstractions, and limits (M&S11-13).
Separates implementation/code verification, per-use solution verification, conceptual validation, empirical validation.
Records verification/validation domains, numerical errors, aspects not verified, uncertainty and sensitivity.
literature.applicability_boundary: General modeling standard; no universal gear-contact error tolerance or automatic certification procedure.
literature.rights_status: Official NASA public-release PDF; no third-party source redistribution in deliverable.

literature.title: ASME V&V 10: Standard for Verification and Validation in Computational Solid Mechanics
literature.reading_scope: Official public product scope and V&V10.1 public description only; paid standard text not obtained.
verified_content: V&V10 supplies common terminology, a conceptual framework and general guidance for computational solid-mechanics VVUQ.
V&V10.1 publicly describes an example-based supplement rather than a substitute for case-specific verification.
literature.applicability_boundary: Not a full-text clause review; cannot claim compliance or infer a numerical acceptance threshold.
literature.rights_status: Copyright ASME; public descriptive pages, paid full text deliberately not downloaded.

literature.title: NAFEMS Code Verification
literature.reading_scope: Public explanatory text and vendor verification table.
verified_content: Vendor benchmark checks are performed by vendors; NAFEMS encourages users to independently verify quoted benchmark results.
literature.applicability_boundary: A benchmark or vendor manual does not prove a new application model or installed binary.
literature.rights_status: NAFEMS copyright; public page read, no member-only manual downloaded.

literature.title: NAFEMS Code Verification Exemplars in Computational Solid Mechanics
literature.identifier: NAFEMS R0135, 2026-03-03; A. van den Bos, P. van der Aa
literature.reading_scope: Public preface, table of contents and bibliographic details only.
verified_content: Rigorous examples estimate observed asymptotic mesh-convergence order using multiple resolutions and an exact solution.
Method can be applied by an end user without source-code access; publication is scoped to linear solid mechanics.
literature.applicability_boundary: Paid/member full text not read; do not transfer linear exact-solution assumptions to changing contact active sets.
literature.rights_status: NAFEMS copyright; only public preface/contents used.

literature.title: Examining Spatial (Grid) Convergence
literature.reading_scope: Public full tutorial: refinement ratio, observed order, asymptotic range, Richardson extrapolation and GCI caveats.
verified_content: Last-two-grid relative difference ignores refinement ratio and order and can be artificially small.
Three grids help estimate order and test asymptotic range; a converged numerical value may still differ from physical truth.
Extrapolation has smoothness/asymptotic assumptions and is invalid locally at discontinuities; near-zero normalization needs another scale.
literature.applicability_boundary: CFD tutorial: transfer convergence reasoning, not its numerical safety factors as universal FEA acceptance gates.
literature.rights_status: Official public NASA technical webpage; cite URL and retrieved hash.

literature.title: Contact stresses in meshing spur gear teeth: Use of an incremental finite element procedure
literature.reading_scope: Abstract, formulation assumptions, semicylinder comparison, spur-gear results and discussion; PDF p13 (printed p11) visually verified.
verified_content: Model is 2D plane strain, small displacement, linearly elastic, with Coulomb friction cases.
Contact extent is unknown a priori and solved incrementally; contact-boundary estimates are more load-increment sensitive than stresses.
The examined gear result was about 10 percent above Hertz pressure; a formula comparison is not universally exact.
literature.applicability_boundary: Old specific models and loading; no claim that its error or mesh is appropriate to current M37.
literature.rights_status: NTRS PUBLIC / GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED; technical text publicly available; no blanket claim all NASA-hosted works are public domain.

literature.title: Effect of extended tooth contact on the modeling of spur gear transmissions
literature.identifier: NASA NTRS 19930019222; Lin, Wang, Oswald, Coy; 1993
literature.reading_scope: Abstract, introduction, loaded-contact formulation and conclusions; PDF p3 visually verified.
verified_content: Elastic tooth deflection can advance entry and delay exit of adjacent tooth pairs.
Ignoring extended contact underestimates contact zone and mean mesh stiffness and overstates individual tooth load, especially for heavily loaded low-contact-ratio gears.
literature.applicability_boundary: Supports an active-contact diagnostic, not automatic attribution of current extra contact to a correct physical mechanism.
literature.rights_status: NTRS public-use access; PDF explicitly credits copyright 1993 H.H. Lin/AIAA with permission. Do not redistribute as public-domain work.

literature.title: Gear Tooth Root Stresses of a Very Heavily Loaded Gear Pair—Case Study: Orbiter Body Flap Actuator Pinion and Ring Gear
literature.identifier: DETC2015-46274; NASA NTRS 20150016602; Krantz and Handschuh; 2015
literature.reading_scope: Abstract, tooth-load/model description, comparison approach and conclusion; PDF p1 visually verified.
verified_content: Undeformed theoretical HPSTC and single-tooth loading can be conservative when deformation changes tooth-to-tooth load sharing.
This specific internal/external pair reported HPSTC-to-contact-analysis maximum-root-stress ratios 1.40 (ring) and 1.28 (pinion).
Coarse system-level meshes were insufficient for local root/fillet stress; refined tooth analysis and load-transfer assumptions matter.
literature.applicability_boundary: Specific heavily loaded actuator pair; ratios are examples, not correction factors for other gears.
literature.rights_status: PDF states U.S. Government work, unrestricted public release; still cite original rather than bundle PDF.

literature.title: Code_Aster SSNV104: Contact de deux sphères
literature.reading_scope: Full public index, reference geometry/material/loading, analytic reference, model A result table and cross-model synthesis.
verified_content: Hertz reference explicitly assumes frictionless contact and contact half-width much smaller than sphere radius.
ANALYTIQUE, NON_REGRESSION and AUTRE_ASTER references are distinguished; locations H/I differ across model variants.
Normal smoothing and geometric contact convergence affect symmetry/pressure; a test comparison must preserve output location and method.
literature.applicability_boundary: Web documentation is retrieved/hash-frozen, not pinned to the independently inspected source commit; document table alone is not current-run evidence.
literature.rights_status: EDF R&D copyrighted public documentation; source test license separately GPL-3.0-or-later.

literature.title: A multi-purpose method for analysis of spur gear tooth loading
literature.reading_scope: NTRS full-text OCR: modeling assumptions, tooth-pair compliance components, loaded-profile iteration and contact/load-sharing discussion around printed pp3,16-17; not every appendix/formula.
verified_content: Tooth-pair deformation includes bending, normal/shear, surrounding hub rocking, rim/hub torsion and local Hertz compliance.
Loaded contact positions, load sharing and stiffness are iterated; a rigid line-of-action contact model has a stated narrower scope.
literature.applicability_boundary: OCR is imperfect and formulas were not transcribed as implementation authority; use for compliance definitions and assumptions, not numeric constants.
literature.rights_status: NTRS public technical report; rights recorded in metadata, no automatic public-domain assumption.

open_source.reading_scope: Hertz formulas and test_hertz fully read; Systems relevant normal-force/contact-area interface inspected.
verified_content: Checks imposed F, displacement, contact area, elastic energy and interior pressure separately with different tolerances.
Hertz energy U=2Fδ/5, not the linear-force law Fδ/2.
open_source.applicability_boundary: FFT elastic-half-space method, not general finite-body FEA or a full gear solver; upstream tests not run.

open_source.reading_scope: Three example definitions, region/BC export instruction, penalty/IPC and nonlinear solver controls.
verified_content: Example explicitly supports exporting regions and EBC nodes without solve.
Linear elastic material and small deformation can still have nonlinear contact.
Penalty stiffness/zero-gap regularization and IPC examples must not be silently treated as hard Hertz contact.
open_source.applicability_boundary: Examples illustrate formulations, not independently verified universal benchmark results; IPC portions explicitly experimental.

open_source.reading_scope: Force-test diagnostics and assertions, MFEM patch displacement tests, README scope and license.
verified_content: Contact search/enforcement are separately parameterized; patch test spans order, search and enforcement choices.
One force test uses abs(F)-abs(pSum)<=tol, a one-sided bound, so do not copy it as an equality/conservation gate.
open_source.applicability_boundary: MFEM-integrated contact library; ENERGY_MORTAR name is not proof of global work-energy balance; all results are static-source findings.

open_source.reading_scope: Card validation/verification loop, load summation coordinates/origin/unsupported branch, selected resultant tests, full license.
verified_content: Checks card fields/references separately from loads resultants; sums F/M about explicit p0 and transforms output coordinates.
Unsupported load types only log warnings before returning partial sums; readiness wrapper must propagate incompleteness.
Full license has three BSD-style redistribution/non-endorsement conditions despite API NOASSERTION.
open_source.applicability_boundary: BDF structure validation does not prove mechanical sufficiency; gravity is optional and defaults false; library does not solve FEA.

open_source.reading_scope: Hertz demo, contact-update/Newton convergence paths and selected custom-kernel comparisons.
verified_content: Separate 2D line/3D sphere Hertz predictions, facet tags, contact quadrature, nonlinear convergence and contact detection updates.
README explicitly describes highly experimental status; Newton failure can raise rather than silently yield accepted output.
open_source.applicability_boundary: FEniCSx/Nitsche implementation; demo-generated analytic pressure is not proof of an assertion or a successful local run.

open_source.reading_scope: Pinned SSNV104 A/B command files, reference result assertions, export settings, copyright/license headers.
verified_content: SSNV104A explicitly compares SIYY analytic -2798.3 with 14% tolerance while preserving separate regression values.
SSNV104B exercises penalty configurations with a distinct 7% analytic criterion; these are example-specific tolerances.
README distinguishes public src from repositories containing proprietary validation/material data.
open_source.applicability_boundary: Do not copy GPL source into a differently licensed stdlib package; implement independent generic rules and cite. Public source differs from any proprietary data collections.
